name: DRV8834 low-voltage stepper motor driver
description: Texas Instruments DRV8834 low-voltage microstepping driver for one bipolar stepper motor: STEP/DIR control with a built-in indexer, full to 1/32 step, adjustable current limit (trimpot, about 1.5 A per coil without cooling, 2 A peak), motor supply 2.5-10.8 V, logic inputs 3.3 V or 5 V (no logic supply pin: the chip powers its logic from VMOT). SLP is pulled LOW in the chip, so it must be driven high. Default (M0/M1 open) is 1/4 step. Sold as: Pololu DRV8834 Low-Voltage Stepper Motor Driver Carrier (#2134, #2874 with headers), 16 pins in two rows: EN M0 M1 (CFG) (REF) SLP STEP DIR, opposite side top to bottom VMOT GND B2 B1 A1 A2 FLT GND.
eli5: Turns a small low-voltage stepper motor exactly one small click every time your board sends it a pulse, in the direction you choose.

pins.name: EN
pins.description: nENBL, active low: low = motor outputs on, high = output stage off (the indexer still counts STEP pulses). 200 kOhm pull-down in the chip, so it is enabled if left open

pins.name: M0
pins.description: M0 microstep select, tri-level (low, high or floating). With M1: M1 M0 = 00 full, 01 1/2, 0Z 1/4, 10 1/8, 11 1/16, 1Z 1/32. Floats by default; float it with a GPIO set as input

pins.name: M1
pins.description: M1 microstep select (200 kOhm pull-down in the chip). Both M0 and M1 open = 1/4 step

pins.name: CFG
pins.description: (CFG) Not connected by default. Bridging a solder jumper connects it to the chip's CONFIG pin (pulled up by 47 kOhm on the board = indexer mode; low = phase/enable mode for two DC motors)

pins.name: REF
pins.description: (REF) Not connected by default. Bridging a solder jumper puts the current-limit reference voltage VREF here (do not drive it)

pins.name: SLP
pins.description: nSLEEP, active low: must be HIGH (>= 2.5 V, max 5.75 V) for the driver to run. 500 kOhm pull-down in the chip, so it sleeps if left open. 10 kOhm to FLT on the board. Wait 1 ms after waking before stepping

pins.name: STEP
pins.description: STEP: each low-to-high edge moves the motor one (micro)step. Min 1.9 us high and 1.9 us low, max 250 kHz. 200 kOhm pull-down

pins.name: DIR
pins.description: DIR: direction, latched on each STEP rising edge (200 ns setup, 1 us hold). 200 kOhm pull-down

pins.name: VMOT
pins.description: Motor supply 2.5-10.8 V (absolute max 11.8 V) from a separate supply, with a >= 47 uF electrolytic capacitor across VMOT/GND close to the board. Also powers the chip's logic (no logic supply pin)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Motor supply ground (printed GND, next to VMOT); joined to the other GND on the board

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Motor coil A, second wire (AOUT2). Connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: FLT
pins.description: nFAULT output: open drain through a 1.5 kOhm resistor, 10 kOhm to SLP on the board. Low on over-current (auto-retry after about 1.2 ms), over-temperature or under-voltage. Safe to tie to a 3.3-5 V logic supply, which then pulls SLP high through the 10 kOhm. Optional

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Logic ground (printed GND, bottom pin next to FLT): connect to the microcontroller GND; joined to the motor GND on the board

supplierQuery: Pololu DRV8834 low-voltage stepper motor driver carrier
buildNotes: One supply: motor VMOT 2.5-10.8 V from a separate supply (for example 2 AA/Li-ion cells, 5 V or 9 V). Never above 10.8 V: the absolute maximum is 11.8 V. The board has no logic supply pin; the chip powers its logic from VMOT, so with VMOT off the driver does nothing. Join the motor supply ground and the microcontroller GND (bottom GND pin).

SLP has a 500 kOhm pull-down in the chip, so the driver sleeps if it is left open. Drive it high from a GPIO (3.3 V is enough: VIH 2.5 V), or tie FLT to 3V3 so the board's 10 kOhm SLP-FLT resistor pulls SLP up. Any external pull-up on SLP must be 4.7 kOhm or less.
Put a 47 uF or larger electrolytic capacitor across VMOT and GND right at the board: LC spikes on long leads can exceed 11.8 V even from a 9 V supply.
Never connect or disconnect the motor while VMOT is powered: it destroys the driver.
Set the current limit before running the motor: Current limit = 2 x VREF (ITRIP = VREF / (5 x 0.1 Ohm)), with VREF measured on the trimpot or the circled 'ref' via. 1 A -> 0.5 V.
Microstepping (M1 M0): 0 0 full, 0 1 half, 0 Z 1/4, 1 0 1/8, 1 1 1/16, 1 Z 1/32 (Z = M0 floating). Left open the board runs at 1/4 step (800 steps per turn of a 200-step motor).
STEP pulses: at least 1.9 us high and 1.9 us low (max 250 kHz); set DIR, M0 and M1 at least 200 ns before the STEP rising edge and hold 1 us after. After SLP goes high wait 1 ms before stepping.
No RESET pin: the (CFG) and (REF) pins are unconnected unless their solder jumpers are bridged. Sleep (SLP low, then high) returns the indexer to home.
sources: https://a.pololu-files.com/picture/0J4345.1200.png (Pololu minimal wiring diagram with pin labels)
https://a.pololu-files.com/picture/0J4350.1200.png (Pololu DRV8834 carrier schematic, header pin numbering)

driver.code:
# DRV8834 low-voltage microstepping bipolar stepper driver (Texas Instruments DRV8834), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the TI DRV8834 datasheet (SLVSB19D) and the Pololu DRV8834 carrier (#2134) schematic.
# The carrier ties CONFIG high (47 kOhm to VINT), so the chip runs in indexer (STEP/DIR) mode.
#   STEP: each LOW->HIGH edge moves the indexer one (micro)step. Min HIGH 1.9 us, min LOW 1.9 us (tWH, tWL),
#         max 250 kHz. 200 kOhm pull-down in the chip.
#   DIR:  direction, latched on the STEP rising edge. Setup 200 ns, hold 1 us (tSU, tH). 200 kOhm pull-down.
#   SLP (nSLEEP, active low): low = sleep, indexer back to home. 500 kOhm pull-down in the chip, so it must be
#         driven HIGH (VIH >= 2.5 V: a 3.3 V GPIO is fine). After waking, wait tWAKE = 1 ms before STEP.
#   EN (nENBL, active low): high = output stage off (the indexer still counts STEP pulses). 200 kOhm pull-down,
#         so enabled if left open.
#   M0 (tri-level: low / high / open) and M1 (200 kOhm pull-down), Table 3, latched on each STEP rising edge:
#         M1 M0: 0 0 full, 0 1 1/2, 0 Z 1/4, 1 0 1/8, 1 1 1/16, 1 Z 1/32. Both open = 1/4 step.
#   FLT (nFAULT): open drain via 1.5 kOhm, 10 kOhm to SLP on the board. Low during over-current (auto-retry
#         after about 1.2 ms), over-temperature, under-voltage, and briefly while waking from sleep.
# There is no RESET pin: sleep (SLP low then high) returns the indexer to its home state.
from machine import Pin
import time

# step divisor -> (M1, M0); M0 = None means high impedance (pin left floating)
_MODES = {1: (0, 0), 2: (0, 1), 4: (0, None), 8: (1, 0), 16: (1, 1), 32: (1, None)}


class DRV8834:
    def __init__(self, step, dir, slp=None, en=None, m0=None, m1=None, flt=None):
        """step, dir: GPIO numbers wired to STEP and DIR.
        slp: GPIO wired to SLP (driven high here). SLP has a pull-down in the chip, so if you pass None you
            must hold it high yourself (e.g. tie FLT to 3V3: the board's 10 kOhm then pulls SLP up).
        en: GPIO wired to EN, or None (the chip's pull-down keeps the outputs enabled).
        m0, m1: GPIOs wired to M0 / M1, or None (left open: 1/4 step).
        flt: GPIO wired to FLT to read faults, or None."""
        self.step_pin = Pin(step, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.dir_pin = Pin(dir, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.en = Pin(en, Pin.OUT, value=0) if en is not None else None
        self.m0 = m0
        self.m1 = Pin(m1, Pin.OUT, value=0) if m1 is not None else None
        if m0 is not None:
            Pin(m0, Pin.IN)  # floating: 1/4 step until set_microstep() is called
        self.flt = Pin(flt, Pin.IN) if flt is not None else None
        self.slp = Pin(slp, Pin.OUT, value=1) if slp is not None else None
        self.position = 0
        time.sleep_ms(2)  # tWAKE <= 1 ms after nSLEEP goes high

    def set_microstep(self, div):
        """div = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. Needs m0 and m1 wired (M0 must be floated for 4 and 32)."""
        if self.m0 is None or self.m1 is None:
            raise ValueError('M0/M1 not wired: board is fixed at 1/4 step')
        m1, m0 = _MODES[div]
        self.m1.value(m1)
        if m0 is None:
            Pin(self.m0, Pin.IN)               # high impedance (no pull) = Z
        else:
            Pin(self.m0, Pin.OUT, value=m0)
        time.sleep_us(1)  # >= 200 ns setup before the next STEP rising edge

    def direction(self, forward):
        """Set DIR (1 = forward). Takes effect on the next STEP rising edge."""
        self.dir_pin.value(1 if forward else 0)
        time.sleep_us(1)  # tSU >= 200 ns

    def step(self, n, delay_us=1000):
        """Move n (micro)steps; n < 0 runs backwards. delay_us = time per step (>= 4)."""
        if n == 0:
            return
        self.direction(n > 0)
        half = max(2, delay_us // 2)
        s = self.step_pin
        for _ in range(abs(n)):
            s.value(1)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tWH >= 1.9 us
            s.value(0)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tWL >= 1.9 us
        time.sleep_us(1)          # tH: keep DIR/M0/M1 1 us after the last rising edge
        self.position += n

    def enable(self, on=True):
        """EN low = outputs on (motor holds torque); EN high = outputs off (indexer still counts steps)."""
        if self.en is not None:
            self.en.value(0 if on else 1)

    def disable(self):
        self.enable(False)

    def sleep(self):
        """SLP low: bridges, charge pump and VINT off (a few uA); indexer resets to home."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(0)

    def wake(self):
        """SLP high, then wait tWAKE (1 ms) before stepping."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(2)

    def fault(self):
        """True while FLT is low (over-current, over-temperature or under-voltage). Needs flt=."""
        return self.flt is not None and self.flt.value() == 0


def vref_for_current(amps, rsense=0.1):
    """VREF (volts on the trimpot / circled 'ref' via) for a full-scale current limit per coil:
    ITRIP = VREF / (5 x Rsense) (datasheet equation 1). The Pololu #2134 uses 0.100 Ohm sense resistors,
    so VREF = amps / 2. The chip still works with VREF below 1 V, with lower accuracy (datasheet note)."""
    return 5 * amps * rsense

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from drv8834 import DRV8834

# STEP/DIR to GPIOs, SLP driven high (it has a pull-down in the chip). M0/M1 left open = 1/4 step.
motor = DRV8834({STEP}, {DIR}, slp={SLP})
while True:
    motor.step(800)           # one revolution of a 1.8 degree motor at 1/4 step
    print('moved 800 microsteps forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.step(-800)
    print('moved 800 microsteps back')
    time.sleep(1)
